dimensions.assessment: Affects students with dyslexia, local educational agencies, and children with disabilities from low-income, low socioeconomic, or limited English proficient backgrounds.
dimensions.evidence: a local educational agency or other agency, in determining eligibility for or providing an accommodation or service under the IDEA, to provide equal access to (1) children from low-income families

dimensions.assessment: Changes statutory definitions and codifies equal access requirements for accommodations and services under IDEA without creating new funding streams.
dimensions.evidence: removes dyslexia from the definition of specific learning disability and establishes a stand-alone definition for dyslexia within the IDEA.

dimensions.assessment: No new federal funding levels or economic appropriations are specified in the source text.
Amends definitions and provisions within the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act governing educational agency responsibilities.
dimensions.evidence: Section 602 of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (20 U.S.C. 1401) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendment to the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act affecting nationwide special education programs.

missing_information: Number of students newly identified or impacted by the stand-alone dyslexia definition is not specified.
Any potential administrative cost adjustments for local educational agencies are not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates a stand-alone definition for dyslexia within the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) and mandates equal access to accommodations for low-income, low socioeconomic status, and limited English proficient children.
